title: बगर बनेको बस्ती र त्रिपालको बास : नुवाकोटको होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा जे देखियो
content:
विदुर (नुवाकोट) । भनिन्छ विपद् बाजा बजाएर आउँदैन । तर, जब आउँछ, यसले पुस्तौँदेखि सिर्जना गरिएको सभ्यता, सम्पत्ति र सपनालाई एकै झट्कामा निमिट्यान्न पारेर जान्छ । भदौ १० गते विभिन्न बस्तीहरूमा यस्तै अकल्पनीय र विनाशकारी विपद् आइलाग्यो । रसुवा र नुवाकोटमा दर्जनौँ बस्ती क्षणभरमै पूर्णरूपमा बगायो । बाढीले सयौँ नागरिकको पुस्तौँदेखि बसोबास गर्दै आएको थातथलो, उर्बर खेतीयोग्य जमिन बगायो । कयौँका आफन्त बाढीले आँखै अगाडि चुँडेर लग्यो । हिजोसम्म आफ्नै घरको आँगनमा भविष्यको तानाबाना बुनिरहेका रसुवाका नागरिक आज छिमेकी जिल्ला नुवाकोटको विदुर नगरपालिका-५ स्थित पिपलटार र कोदोबारीमा अस्थायी होल्डिङ सेन्टरहरूमा त्रिपालमुनि शरण लिन बाध्य छन् । आफ्नो सर्वस्व गुमाएका यी नागरिकहरूको वर्तमान जति कष्टकर छ, भविष्य त्योभन्दा पनि बढी अनिश्चित र कहालीलाग्दो देखिन्छ । नेपाल प्रेस ले यी होल्डिङ सेन्टरहरूमा पुगेर गरेको स्थलगत अध्ययन, प्रभावितका पीडा र भोगाइको अवलोकन, जनप्रतिनिधिहरूसँगको संवादलगायतको वस्तुस्थिति विश्लेषण गरेको छ । रसुवाका बाढीपीडितहरूलाई तत्काल आपत्कालीन राहत, गाँस र बासको प्रबन्ध मिलाउन नुवाकोटको विदुर नगरपालिका, नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी, सेभ द चिल्ड्रेन र विश्व खाद्य कार्यक्रमजस्ता संस्थाहरूको संयुक्त सहकार्यमा दुईवटा होल्डिङ सेन्टर सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएका छन् । पिपलटारको होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा उत्तरगया गाउँपालिकाको खाल्टेका बाढी प्रभावितलाई राखिएको छ। यहाँ कुल ३० वटा टेन्टमा १२० जना बसिरहेका छन् । राहत वितरण गर्ने संस्थाहरूले रासन उपलब्ध गराउँछन् र प्रभावितहरूले आ-आफ्नो समूह बनाइ एकै परिवार जस्तै आफैँ पकाएर खान्छन् । नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीकी स्वयंसेवक ऐश्वर्या पुडासैनीका अनुसार यस सेन्टरमा बालबालिका र महिलाहरूको मानसिक स्वास्थ्यलाई मध्यनजर गर्दै उनीहरूलाई सहज बनाउन र मनोसामाजिक परामर्श (काउन्सिलिङ) प्रदान गर्न छुट्टै ‘महिला मैत्री केन्द्र’ समेत स्थापना गरिएको छ । अर्का रेडक्रसकर्मी ऋषि रिजाल यहाँ राखिएकाहरूलाई स्वयंसेवकले पिउने पानी, रासन, त्रिपाल तथा भान्सा व्यवस्थापनको निरन्तर समन्वय गरिरहेका छन्। सुरक्षा संवेदनशीलतालाई ध्यानमा राख्दै बाहिरी अनाधिकृत व्यक्तिहरूको प्रवेश रोक्न सेन्टरको वरिपरि बाँसको बार लगाइएको छ र मुख्य गेट निर्माण गरिएको छ । पिपलटारभन्दा केही पर कोदोबारी होल्डिङ सेन्टर रहेको छ । विदुर-५ का वडाध्यक्षको निजी जग्गा भाडामा लिएर झाडी र पाक्न लागेको कोदोको बोट फाँडेर आपत्कालीन रूपमा सेन्टर सञ्चालनमा ल्याइयो यहाँ रसुवाको आमाछोदिङ्मो गाउँपालिकासहित बाढीग्रस्त क्षेत्रका ७७ घरपरिवारका २७३ जना सदस्यलाई राखिएको छ । यस सेन्टरमा विश्व खाद्य कार्यक्रमको सहयोगमा सामूहिक मेस चलाइएको छ, जहाँ सबैका लागि सामूहिक रूपमा खाना पकाइन्छ र वितरण गरिन्छ । नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी नुवाकोटका प्रतिनिधि विनोद लामिछानेका अनुसार यहाँको जनसङ्ख्या धेरै भएकाले स्वास्थ्य जोखिम पनि उच्च छ । त्यसैले, चौबीसै घण्टा सेवा दिने गरी एम्बुलेन्स र ५-६ जना तालिमप्राप्त स्वयंसेवकहरूलाई तयारी अवस्थामा राखिएको छ । साथै, सुरक्षित खानेपानी, अस्थायी शौचालय, धारा र प्राथमिक स्वास्थ्य उपचारको पर्याप्त प्रबन्ध मिलाउने प्रयास गरिएको छ । आँखाअगाडि परिवार बग्दाको पीडा उत्तरगया गाउँपालिका- १ का उचङ आलेको अनुहारमा बाढीले मानिसलाई कतिसम्म निरीह बनाउँछ भन्ने भाव प्रष्ट झल्किन्छ । श्रीमती, छोराबुहारीसमेत गरी उनको परिवारका ४ जना सदस्य आँखाअगाडि बाढीले बगायो । उनी भन्छन्, ‘मेरो आँखै अगाडि सबैलाई लग्यो । बचाउन अन्तिमसम्म तानेँ, तर पानीको भेल यति ठूलो थियो कि हात खुस्केर गयो । उनीहरूलाई पानीले निल्यो, म हेरेको हेरै भएँ ।’ झण्डै १ सय भेडा पालेर राम्रै जीवनयापन गरिरहेका उनको गोठ पनि बाढीले लग्यो । भाग्यवश बचेका केही भेडाहरू गाउँमै सस्तोमा बेच्नुपर्यो र अहिले एक्लै त्रिपालको आश्रयमा दिन काटिरहेका छन् । ‘अहिले न मेरो घर छ, न भेडा छन्, न त मैले टेकेको माटो नै बाँकी छ । बाढीले सबै बगाएर बगर बनाइदियो,’ काम गर्न पनि मन लाग्दैन अब त । काठमाडौंमा १२ कक्षा पढिरहेका सुब्बा तामाङ बाढी आउँदा काठमाडौंमै थिए । उनी समाचार सुन्नासा गाउँ फर्किए । उनको परिवारसहित सिङ्गो गाउँ भूकम्पपछि नुवाकोटको बेत्रावती नजिकैको साल्ती र खाल्टेमा सरेको थियो । तर, नियतिको खेल बल्लबल्ल बसालेको नयाँ बस्ती पनि पूर्ण रूपमा बाढीले बगायो । तामाङका कान्छा काकाको परिवारका ५ जनामध्ये ४ जना र दुईटी फुपूको परिवारका ४ जना गरी ८ जना आफन्तले ज्यान गुमाए । ‘भूकम्पपछि गाउँ छाडेर यहाँ बस्यौँ, शून्यबाट जीवन सुरु गरेका थियौँ । तर अहिले बाढीले त्यो पनि सिध्यायो,’ उनी भन्छन्, ‘आफन्तहरू धेरै गुमायौँ । हिजो भर्खर गएर पुरानो गाउँ हेर्न जाँदा भूगोल नै पुरै उल्टिएको छ । घर भएको ठाउँमा खोला बगेको छ । नमिठो सपना जस्तै लाग्छ ।’ बाढी आएका बेला रसुवाका धेरैजना रोजगारी वा व्यापारको सिलसिलामा चीनको केरुङ पुगेका थिए । तीमध्ये एक स्थानीय वृद्धाको अनुभव झनै कष्टकर छ । रसुवागढी नाकाको मितेरी पुल र सडक सञ्जाल बगाएपछि उनी चीनतर्फ नै थुनिइन् । उनी ल्हासा र सिन्धुपाल्चोक हुँदै गाडी र पैदल यात्रा गरेर ६-७ दिनको निरन्तर कष्टकर यात्रापछि मात्र नुवाकोट आइपुगिन् । आफ्नो परिवार जीवितै देख्दा राहतको सास फेरिन् । अहिले उनी आफ्ना ७ जना परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग एउटै त्रिपालमुनि आश्रय लिइरहेकी छन् । कोदोबारी सेन्टरमा बसिरहेकी याङजिन तामाङ गाउँबाट भाग्दा ज्यानसँगै जोगाएर ल्याएको पुरानो धागो र सियोबाट परम्परागत पहिरन ‘कुने’ (महिलाहरूले कपडाको पछाडि बाँध्ने विशेष प्रकारको कपडा) बुनेर मन बहलााइरहेको भेटिइन् । होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा नेपाल रेडक्रस, विदुर नगरपालिका लगायतका मानवीय संघसंस्थाहरूले गाँस र बासको तत्कालीन प्रबन्ध गरे तापनि त्रिपालको बसाइ जति दिन लम्बियो, त्यति नै नयाँ समस्याहरू थपिँदै गएका छन् । बाढीले घरसँगै बालबालिकाको विद्यालय र किताबकापी पनि बगायो । होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा रहेका स्कुल जाने उमेरका बालबालिकाहरूको पढाइ नबिग्रियोस् भनेर उनीहरूलाई नजिकैका स्थानीय विद्यालयमा भर्ना गराई पढाउन पठाइएको छ । सेभ द चिल्ड्रेन र रेडक्रसको सहजीकरणमा केही स्वयंसेवकले बिहान र बेलुका १-१ घण्टा बालबालिकालाई त्रिपालमुनि अतिरिक्त कक्षा पढाउने र गृहकार्य गराइरहेका छन् । स्वयंसेवक एन्जला तामाङ भन्छिन्, ‘बालबालिकाहरू स्कुल त गएका छन्, तर घरमा आएर पढ्न किताब नै छैन। घरसँगै सबै किताब बगेकाले अभ्यास गर्न र होमवर्क गर्न निकै समस्या परेको छ ।’ यसबाहेक उनीहरू गम्भीर मनोसामाजिक आघातबाट गुज्रिरहेका छन् । असोज १० को त्यो भयानक रातको घटना सम्झँदा उनीहरू अझै तर्सिने, निद्रामा आत्तिने, चिच्याउने र अभिभावक वा साथीभाइ गुमाएको शोकमा एक्कासि भावुक हुने समस्या व्याप्त छ । त्रिपालको बसोबासका कारण सबैभन्दा बढी कष्ट महिला, किशोरी र सुत्केरीहरूले भोग्नुपरेको छ । रसुवाको चिसो हावापानीमा हुर्केका उनीहरूलाई नुवाकोटको तातो वातावरण त्यसै पनि कष्टकर छ । त्यसमाथि त्रिपालमुनिको साँघुरो र खुला वातावरणमा नुहाउन, शौच गर्न र कपडा फेर्न असहज मान्ने गरेका छन् । रेडक्रसले अलग्गै स्थानको व्यवस्था भने गरेको छ । पिपलटार होल्डिङ सेन्टरको नजिकैको सुँगुर फार्मबाट गर्मी र हावा चलेको समयमा त्यहाँबाट आउने तीव्र दुर्गन्धका कारण सास फेर्न सास्ती भइरहेको प्रभावितहरू बताउँछन् । चिसो मौसम सुरु भइसकेको छ । रातको समयमा शीत खस्ने र भुइँबाट चिसो आउने हुनाले त्रिपालमुनिको बसाइ अत्यन्तै जोखिमपूर्ण बन्दै गएको छ । बालबालिका र वृद्धवृद्धाहरू रुघाखोकी र निमोनियाको सिकार हुन थालेका छन् । रेडक्रसका प्रतिनिधि विनोद लामिछानेका अनुसार चिसोबाट बचाउन पुराना र पातला त्रिपालहरू बदलेर न्यानो टेन्ट तथा जस्तापाता (टिन) को अस्थायी छाप्रो निर्माणतर्फ पहल भइरहेको छ, तर स्रोतको अभावले यो काम द्रुत गतिमा अघि बढ्न सकेको छैन । होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा दिइएको अस्थायी राहतले तत्कालको गर्जो त टारेको छ, तर बाढीपीडितहरूको भविष्य चरम अनिश्चिततामा रुमल्लिएको छ । उत्तरगया गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्ष माधवप्रसाद अर्याल पुन: बस्ती बसाउन मिल्ने सार्वजनिक जग्गासमेत पालिकामा छैन । भूगोल नै क्षतविक्षत भएकाले पीडितहरूलाई साविककै ठाउँमा फर्काउन असम्भवप्रायः छ । यस विषम परिस्थितिमा, दातृ निकायको भर परेर मात्र पुग्दैन । राज्यका तीनै तहका सरकारले रणनीतिक रूपमा योजना अगाडि बढाउनुपर्छ । सरकारले तत्काल भौगर्भिक अध्ययन गरी सुरक्षित स्थान खोजी गरी एकीकृत बस्ती बनाउनुपर्ने, बाढीले नागरिकता, लालपुर्जा, विद्यार्थीका शैक्षिक प्रमाणपत्रलगायतका महत्वपूर्ण कागजात होल्डिङ सेन्टरमै घुम्ती शिविर चलाएर पुनः जारी गर्नुपर्छ । कृषियोग्य जमिन नभएकोले उनीहरूलाई विभिन्न सीपमार्फत् वैकल्पिक पेसातर्फ आकर्षित गर्नुपर्छ । जसका लागि सहुलीयतपूर्ण ऋण र बीउपुँजी अनुदानको रूपमा उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्ने सरोकारवालाले बताएका छन् । प्रभावित बालबालिकाहरूका लागि निःशुल्क शैक्षिक सामग्री र अभिभावक गुमाएकाहरूलाई उच्च शिक्षासम्म नि:शुल्क ग्यारेन्टी गर्नुपर्छ । नेपाल रेडक्रस नुवाकोटका अध्यक्ष हरि श्रेष्ठ परिवारका सदस्य गुमाएकाहरू गहिरो मानसिक आघात, शोक र भविष्यको चिन्ताले डिप्रेसन र एन्जाइटीको समस्या बढ्न थालेको बताउँछन् । यसलाई बेलैमैमा सम्बोधन गर्न आवश्यक रहेको उनको भनाइ छ । पिपलटार र कोदोबारी होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा पाएको आपत्कालीन आश्रय, भोजन र मानवीय सहायताले तत्कालीन राहत त दिएको छ । सँगसँगै राज्यको बलियो उपस्थिति, अभिभावकत्व र न्यानो भरोसाको खाँचो छ । आफ्नो जन्मथलो, पैतृक सम्पत्ति, जीवनभरको कमाइ र आफ्ना प्रियजनहरू गुमाएर चरम अनिश्चित भविष्यको सामना गरिरहेका यी नागरिक अहिले राज्यको मुख ताकेर बसेका छन् । उनीहरूका लागि तत्काल स्थायी पुनर्वास, भू-स्वामित्वसहित जग्गा व्यवस्थापन, जीविकोपार्जनको ग्यारेन्टी गरिनुपर्छ । Bidur (Nuwakot). It is said that disaster does not come with a bang. But, when it comes, it wipes out the civilization, wealth and dreams created over generations in one fell swoop. On Bhadra 10, such an unimaginable and devastating disaster struck various settlements. Dozens of settlements in Rasuwa and Nuwakot were completely swept away in an instant. The flood washed away the fertile farmlands and homes where hundreds of citizens had lived for generations. Many relatives were swept away before their eyes. The citizens of Rasuwa, who were weaving the fabric of their future in their own backyards until yesterday, are now forced to take shelter under tarpaulins in temporary holding centers in Pipaltar and Kodobari, located in Bidur Municipality-5 of the neighboring district of Nuwakot. As difficult as the present is for these citizens who have lost everything, the future seems even more uncertain and dire. Nepal Press has analyzed the situation through on-site studies conducted at these holding centers, observations of the pain and suffering of those affected, and dialogue with public representatives. Two holding centers have been put into operation in collaboration with Bidur Municipality of Nuwakot, Nepal Red Cross Society, Save the Children, and the World Food Program to provide immediate emergency relief, food, and shelter to flood victims in Rasuwa. The holding center in Pipaltar is housing flood victims from Khalte, Uttargaya Rural Municipality. A total of 120 people are living here in 30 tents. Relief organizations provide rations, and the affected people form their own groups and cook and eat like a family. According to Aishwarya Pudasaini, a volunteer at the Nepal Red Cross Society, a separate 'Women-Friendly Center' has also been established at this center to provide psychosocial counseling and to make children and women feel comfortable, keeping in mind their mental health. Another Red Cross worker, Rishi Rijal, is continuously coordinating the provision of drinking water, rations, tarpaulins and kitchen management by volunteers for those housed here. Keeping in mind the security sensitivity, a bamboo fence has been erected around the center to prevent the entry of unauthorized persons from outside and a main gate has been constructed. A little further from Pipaltar is the Kodobari Holding Center. The center was brought into operation on an emergency basis by renting the private land of the ward chairman of Bidur-5, uprooting bushes and ripening millet plants. This center houses 273 members of 77 households from flood-affected areas, including Amachodingmo Rural Municipality in Rasuwa. A communal mess is run at this center with the support of the World Food Program, where food is cooked and distributed collectively for everyone. According to Binod Lamichhane, representative of Nepal Red Cross Society Nuwakot, the health risk is also high due to the large population here. Therefore, an ambulance and 5-6 trained volunteers have been kept on standby to provide 24-hour service. In addition, efforts have been made to make adequate arrangements for safe drinking water, temporary toilets, taps and primary health care. The pain of seeing a family disappear before our eyes The face of Uchang Ale of Uttargaya Rural Municipality-1 clearly reflects the extent to which floods make people helpless. Four members of his family, including his wife, son and daughter-in-law, were swept away by the flood before his eyes. He says, "They all disappeared before my eyes. I pulled to the end to save them, but the water was so strong that my hand slipped. They were swallowed by the water, and I was stunned." His sheepfold, where he was earning a good living by raising about 100 sheep, was also washed away by the flood. Fortunately, the few remaining sheep had to be sold cheaply in the village and are now spending their days alone under the shelter of a tent. "Now I have neither a house, nor sheep, nor the soil I used to walk on. The flood washed everything away and turned it into a wasteland," he says, "I don't even feel like working anymore." Subba Tamang, who was studying in grade 12 in Kathmandu, was in Kathmandu when the floods hit. He returned to his village after hearing the news. His entire village, including his family, had moved to Salti and Khalte near Betrawati in Nuwakot after the earthquake. However, as fate would have it, the newly built settlement was completely swept away by the flood. Eight relatives, including four out of five members of Tamang's younger uncle's family and four members of his aunt's family, lost their lives. "We left the village after the earthquake and settled here, starting life from scratch. But now the flood has ended that too," he says. "We have lost many relatives. Just yesterday, when I went to see the old village, the geography was completely turned upside down. A river has flowed where the house used to be. It feels like a bitter dream." When the floods hit, many people from Rasuwa had reached Kerung, China, for employment or business. The experience of one of them, an elderly local woman, is even more painful. She was stranded on the Chinese side after the Miteri Bridge and road network at the Rasuwagadhi border were washed away. She reached Nuwakot only after 6-7 days of continuous and arduous journey by car and on foot via Lhasa and Sindhupalchowk. She breathed a sigh of relief when she saw her family alive. She is now sheltering under a tent with her 7 family members. Yangjin Tamang, who lives in the Kodobari Center, was found entertaining herself by weaving a traditional garment called a 'kune' (a special type of cloth that women tie at the back of their clothes) using old threads and needles she had brought with her when she fled her village. Although humanitarian organizations including the Nepal Red Cross and Bidur Municipality made immediate arrangements for food and shelter at the holding center, new problems have been added as the tents' stay has prolonged. The flood washed away the children's school and textbooks along with their homes. To ensure that the school-age children in the holding center do not suffer, they have been admitted to nearby local schools and sent to study. With the facilitation of Save the Children and the Red Cross, some volunteers are teaching extra classes and doing homework for children under a tent for 1 hour each in the morning and evening. Volunteer Angela Tamang says, "The children have gone to school, but they don't have any books to read when they come home. Since all the books have gone with them, it's been very difficult to practice and do homework." In addition, they are going through severe psychosocial trauma. When they remember the terrible night of Asosh 10, they still experience fear, sleeplessness, screaming, and sudden emotional outbursts in grief over the loss of a parent or friend. Women, adolescents and pregnant women have suffered the most due to living in tents. Having grown up in the cold climate of Rasuwa, the hot environment of Nuwakot is also difficult for them. Moreover, they find it uncomfortable to bathe, defecate and change clothes in the cramped and open environment under the tents. The Red Cross has arranged a separate place. Those affected say they are having difficulty breathing due to the strong odor emanating from the pig farm near the Pipaltar Holding Center during hot and windy weather. The cold season has begun. As frost falls at night and the ground is cold, staying under tarpaulins has become extremely risky. Children and the elderly are becoming victims of colds and pneumonia. According to Red Cross representative Binod Lamichhane, efforts are being made to replace old and thin tarpaulins with warm tents and temporary shelters made of tin sheets to protect against the cold, but this work has not progressed quickly due to lack of resources. The temporary relief provided at the holding center has alleviated the immediate crisis, but the future of the flood victims is shrouded in extreme uncertainty. Uttargaya Rural Municipality Chairman Madhav Prasad Aryal said that the municipality does not even have public land that can be used for resettlement. Since the geography itself is damaged, it is almost impossible to return the victims to their previous places. In this critical situation, relying solely on donor agencies is not enough. All three levels of government must strategically advance the plan. The government should immediately conduct a geological study, find a safe location, and build an integrated settlement. Important documents such as citizenship, red papers, and students' educational certificates should be reissued at the holding center by running mobile camps. Since there is no arable land, they should be attracted towards alternative professions through various skills. For this, stakeholders have said that concessional loans and seed capital should be provided in the form of grants. Free educational materials should be guaranteed for affected children and free higher education for those who have lost their parents. Hari Shrestha, president of Nepal Red Cross Nuwakot, says that those who have lost family members are experiencing increased depression and anxiety due to deep mental trauma, grief, and worries about the future. He says that this needs to be addressed promptly. The emergency shelter, food, and humanitarian assistance provided at Pipaltar and Kodobari Holding Centers have provided immediate relief. At the same time, there is a need for a strong state presence, guardianship, and warm trust. These citizens, who have lost their birthplace, ancestral property, life's earnings, and loved ones, and are facing an extremely uncertain future, are now looking to the state for immediate permanent resettlement, land management, including land ownership, and guaranteed livelihoods.

विदुर (नुवाकोट) । भनिन्छ विपद् बाजा बजाएर आउँदैन । तर, जब आउँछ, यसले पुस्तौँदेखि सिर्जना गरिएको सभ्यता, सम्पत्ति र सपनालाई एकै झट्कामा निमिट्यान्न पारेर जान्छ । भदौ १० गते विभिन्न बस्तीहरूमा यस्तै अकल्पनीय र विनाशकारी विपद् आइलाग्यो । रसुवा र नुवाकोटमा दर्जनौँ बस्ती क्षणभरमै पूर्णरूपमा बगायो । बाढीले सयौँ नागरिकको पुस्तौँदेखि बसोबास गर्दै आएको थातथलो, उर्बर खेतीयोग्य जमिन बगायो । कयौँका आफन्त बाढीले आँखै अगाडि चुँडेर लग्यो । हिजोसम्म आफ्नै घरको आँगनमा भविष्यको तानाबाना बुनिरहेका रसुवाका नागरिक आज छिमेकी जिल्ला नुवाकोटको विदुर नगरपालिका-५ स्थित पिपलटार र कोदोबारीमा अस्थायी होल्डिङ सेन्टरहरूमा त्रिपालमुनि शरण लिन बाध्य छन् । आफ्नो सर्वस्व गुमाएका यी नागरिकहरूको वर्तमान जति कष्टकर छ, भविष्य त्योभन्दा पनि बढी अनिश्चित र कहालीलाग्दो देखिन्छ । नेपाल प्रेस ले यी होल्डिङ सेन्टरहरूमा पुगेर गरेको स्थलगत अध्ययन, प्रभावितका पीडा र भोगाइको अवलोकन, जनप्रतिनिधिहरूसँगको संवादलगायतको वस्तुस्थिति विश्लेषण गरेको छ । रसुवाका बाढीपीडितहरूलाई तत्काल आपत्कालीन राहत, गाँस र बासको प्रबन्ध मिलाउन नुवाकोटको विदुर नगरपालिका, नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी, सेभ द चिल्ड्रेन र विश्व खाद्य कार्यक्रमजस्ता संस्थाहरूको संयुक्त सहकार्यमा दुईवटा होल्डिङ सेन्टर सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएका छन् । पिपलटारको होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा उत्तरगया गाउँपालिकाको खाल्टेका बाढी प्रभावितलाई राखिएको छ। यहाँ कुल ३० वटा टेन्टमा १२० जना बसिरहेका छन् । राहत वितरण गर्ने संस्थाहरूले रासन उपलब्ध गराउँछन् र प्रभावितहरूले आ-आफ्नो समूह बनाइ एकै परिवार जस्तै आफैँ पकाएर खान्छन् । नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीकी स्वयंसेवक ऐश्वर्या पुडासैनीका अनुसार यस सेन्टरमा बालबालिका र महिलाहरूको मानसिक स्वास्थ्यलाई मध्यनजर गर्दै उनीहरूलाई सहज बनाउन र मनोसामाजिक परामर्श (काउन्सिलिङ) प्रदान गर्न छुट्टै ‘महिला मैत्री केन्द्र’ समेत स्थापना गरिएको छ । अर्का रेडक्रसकर्मी ऋषि रिजाल यहाँ राखिएकाहरूलाई स्वयंसेवकले पिउने पानी, रासन, त्रिपाल तथा भान्सा व्यवस्थापनको निरन्तर समन्वय गरिरहेका छन्। सुरक्षा संवेदनशीलतालाई ध्यानमा राख्दै बाहिरी अनाधिकृत व्यक्तिहरूको प्रवेश रोक्न सेन्टरको वरिपरि बाँसको बार लगाइएको छ र मुख्य गेट निर्माण गरिएको छ । पिपलटारभन्दा केही पर कोदोबारी होल्डिङ सेन्टर रहेको छ । विदुर-५ का वडाध्यक्षको निजी जग्गा भाडामा लिएर झाडी र पाक्न लागेको कोदोको बोट फाँडेर आपत्कालीन रूपमा सेन्टर सञ्चालनमा ल्याइयो यहाँ रसुवाको आमाछोदिङ्मो गाउँपालिकासहित बाढीग्रस्त क्षेत्रका ७७ घरपरिवारका २७३ जना सदस्यलाई राखिएको छ । यस सेन्टरमा विश्व खाद्य कार्यक्रमको सहयोगमा सामूहिक मेस चलाइएको छ, जहाँ सबैका लागि सामूहिक रूपमा खाना पकाइन्छ र वितरण गरिन्छ । नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी नुवाकोटका प्रतिनिधि विनोद लामिछानेका अनुसार यहाँको जनसङ्ख्या धेरै भएकाले स्वास्थ्य जोखिम पनि उच्च छ । त्यसैले, चौबीसै घण्टा सेवा दिने गरी एम्बुलेन्स र ५-६ जना तालिमप्राप्त स्वयंसेवकहरूलाई तयारी अवस्थामा राखिएको छ । साथै, सुरक्षित खानेपानी, अस्थायी शौचालय, धारा र प्राथमिक स्वास्थ्य उपचारको पर्याप्त प्रबन्ध मिलाउने प्रयास गरिएको छ । आँखाअगाडि परिवार बग्दाको पीडा उत्तरगया गाउँपालिका- १ का उचङ आलेको अनुहारमा बाढीले मानिसलाई कतिसम्म निरीह बनाउँछ भन्ने भाव प्रष्ट झल्किन्छ । श्रीमती, छोराबुहारीसमेत गरी उनको परिवारका ४ जना सदस्य आँखाअगाडि बाढीले बगायो । उनी भन्छन्, ‘मेरो आँखै अगाडि सबैलाई लग्यो । बचाउन अन्तिमसम्म तानेँ, तर पानीको भेल यति ठूलो थियो कि हात खुस्केर गयो । उनीहरूलाई पानीले निल्यो, म हेरेको हेरै भएँ ।’ झण्डै १ सय भेडा पालेर राम्रै जीवनयापन गरिरहेका उनको गोठ पनि बाढीले लग्यो । भाग्यवश बचेका केही भेडाहरू गाउँमै सस्तोमा बेच्नुपर्यो र अहिले एक्लै त्रिपालको आश्रयमा दिन काटिरहेका छन् । ‘अहिले न मेरो घर छ, न भेडा छन्, न त मैले टेकेको माटो नै बाँकी छ । बाढीले सबै बगाएर बगर गाउँ हेर्न जाँदा भूगोल नै पुरै उल्टिएको छ । घर भएको ठाउँमा खोला बगेको छ । नमिठो सपना जस्तै लाग्छ ।’ बाढी आएका बेला रसुवाका धेरैजना रोजगारी वा व्यापारको सिलसिलामा चीनको केरुङ पुगेका थिए । तीमध्ये एक स्थानीय वृद्धाको अनुभव झनै कष्टकर छ । रसुवागढी नाकाको मितेरी पुल र सडक सञ्जाल बगाएपछि उनी चीनतर्फ नै थुनिइन् । उनी ल्हासा र सिन्धुपाल्चोक हुँदै गाडी र पैदल यात्रा गरेर ६-७ दिनको निरन्तर कष्टकर यात्रापछि मात्र नुवाकोट आइपुगिन् । आफ्नो परिवार जीवितै देख्दा राहतको सास फेरिन् । अहिले उनी आफ्ना ७ जना परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग एउटै त्रिपालमुनि आश्रय लिइरहेकी छन् । कोदोबारी सेन्टरमा बसिरहेकी याङजिन तामाङ गाउँबाट भाग्दा ज्यानसँगै जोगाएर ल्याएको पुरानो धागो र सियोबाट परम्परागत पहिरन ‘कुने’ (महिलाहरूले कपडाको पछाडि बाँध्ने विशेष प्रकारको कपडा) बुनेर मन बहलााइरहेको भेटिइन् । होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा नेपाल रेडक्रस, विदुर नगरपालिका लगायतका मानवीय संघसंस्थाहरूले गाँस र बासको तत्कालीन प्रबन्ध गरे तापनि त्रिपालको बसाइ जति दिन लम्बियो, त्यति नै नयाँ समस्याहरू थपिँदै गएका छन् । बाढीले घरसँगै बालबालिकाको विद्यालय र किताबकापी पनि बगायो । होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा रहेका स्कुल जाने उमेरका बालबालिकाहरूको पढाइ नबिग्रियोस् भनेर उनीहरूलाई नजिकैका स्थानीय विद्यालयमा भर्ना गराई पढाउन पठाइएको छ । सेभ द चिल्ड्रेन र रेडक्रसको सहजीकरणमा केही स्वयंसेवकले बिहान र बेलुका १-१ घण्टा बालबालिकालाई त्रिपालमुनि अतिरिक्त कक्षा पढाउने र गृहकार्य गराइरहेका छन् । स्वयंसेवक एन्जला तामाङ भन्छिन्, ‘बालबालिकाहरू स्कुल त गएका छन्, तर घरमा आएर पढ्न किताब नै छैन। घरसँगै सबै किताब बगेकाले अभ्यास गर्न र होमवर्क गर्न निकै समस्या परेको छ ।’ यसबाहेक उनीहरू गम्भीर मनोसामाजिक आघातबाट गुज्रिरहेका छन् । असोज १० को त्यो भयानक रातको घटना सम्झँदा उनीहरू अझै तर्सिने, निद्रामा आत्तिने, चिच्याउने र अभिभावक वा साथीभाइ गुमाएको शोकमा एक्कासि भावुक हुने समस्या व्याप्त छ । त्रिपालको बसोबासका कारण सबैभन्दा बढी कष्ट महिला, किशोरी र सुत्केरीहरूले भोग्नुपरेको छ । रसुवाको चिसो हावापानीमा हुर्केका उनीहरूलाई नुवाकोटको तातो वातावरण त्यसै पनि कष्टकर छ । त्यसमाथि त्रिपालमुनिको साँघुरो र खुला वातावरणमा नुहाउन, शौच गर्न र कपडा फेर्न असहज मान्ने गरेका छन् । रेडक्रसले अलग्गै स्थानको व्यवस्था भने गरेको छ । पिपलटार होल्डिङ सेन्टरको नजिकैको सुँगुर फार्मबाट गर्मी र हावा चलेको समयमा त्यहाँबाट आउने तीव्र दुर्गन्धका कारण सास फेर्न सास्ती भइरहेको प्रभावितहरू बताउँछन् । चिसो मौसम सुरु भइसकेको छ । रातको समयमा शीत खस्ने र भुइँबाट चिसो आउने हुनाले त्रिपालमुनिको बसाइ अत्यन्तै जोखिमपूर्ण बन्दै गएको छ । बालबालिका र वृद्धवृद्धाहरू रुघाखोकी र निमोनियाको सिकार हुन थालेका छन् । रेडक्रसका प्रतिनिधि विनोद लामिछानेका अनुसार चिसोबाट बचाउन पुराना र पातला त्रिपालहरू बदलेर न्यानो टेन्ट तथा जस्तापाता (टिन) को अस्थायी छाप्रो निर्माणतर्फ पहल भइरहेको छ, तर स्रोतको अभावले यो काम द्रुत गतिमा अघि बढ्न सकेको छैन । होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा दिइएको अस्थायी राहतले तत्कालको गर्जो त टारेको छ, तर बाढीपीडितहरूको भविष्य चरम अनिश्चिततामा रुमल्लिएको छ । उत्तरगया गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्ष माधवप्रसाद अर्याल पुन: बस्ती बसाउन मिल्ने सार्वजनिक जग्गासमेत पालिकामा छैन । भूगोल नै क्षतविक्षत भएकाले पीडितहरूलाई साविककै ठाउँमा फर्काउन असम्भवप्रायः छ । यस विषम परिस्थितिमा, दातृ निकायको भर परेर मात्र पुग्दैन । राज्यका तीनै तहका सरकारले रणनीतिक रूपमा योजना अगाडि बढाउनुपर्छ । सरकारले तत्काल भौगर्भिक अध्ययन गरी सुरक्षित स्थान खोजी गरी एकीकृत बस्ती बनाउनुपर्ने, बाढीले नागरिकता, लालपुर्जा, विद्यार्थीका शैक्षिक प्रमाणपत्रलगायतका महत्वपूर्ण कागजात होल्डिङ सेन्टरमै घुम्ती शिविर चलाएर पुनः जारी गर्नुपर्छ । कृषियोग्य जमिन नभएकोले उनीहरूलाई विभिन्न सीपमार्फत् वैकल्पिक पेसातर्फ आकर्षित गर्नुपर्छ । जसका लागि सहुलीयतपूर्ण ऋण र बीउपुँजी अनुदानको रूपमा उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्ने सरोकारवालाले बताएका छन् । प्रभावित बालबालिकाहरूका लागि निःशुल्क शैक्षिक सामग्री र अभिभावक गुमाएकाहरूलाई उच्च शिक्षासम्म नि:शुल्क ग्यारेन्टी गर्नुपर्छ । नेपाल रेडक्रस नुवाकोटका अध्यक्ष हरि श्रेष्ठ परिवारका सदस्य गुमाएकाहरू गहिरो मानसिक आघात, शोक र भविष्यको चिन्ताले डिप्रेसन र एन्जाइटीको समस्या बढ्न थालेको बताउँछन् । यसलाई बेलैमैमा सम्बोधन गर्न आवश्यक रहेको उनको भनाइ छ । पिपलटार र कोदोबारी होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा पाएको आपत्कालीन आश्रय, भोजन र मानवीय सहायताले तत्कालीन राहत त दिएको छ । सँगसँगै राज्यको बलियो उपस्थिति, अभिभावकत्व र न्यानो भरोसाको खाँचो छ । आफ्नो जन्मथलो, पैतृक सम्पत्ति, जीवनभरको कमाइ र आफ्ना प्रियजनहरू गुमाएर चरम अनिश्चित भविष्यको सामना गरिरहेका यी नागरिक अहिले राज्यको मुख ताकेर बसेका छन् । उनीहरूका लागि तत्काल स्थायी पुनर्वास, भू-स्वामित्वसहित जग्गा व्यवस्थापन, जीविकोपार्जनको ग्यारेन्टी गरिनुपर्छ ।

विदुर (नुवाकोट) । भनिन्छ विपद् बाजा बजाएर आउँदैन । तर, जब आउँछ, यसले पुस्तौँदेखि सिर्जना गरिएको सभ्यता, सम्पत्ति र सपनालाई एकै झट्कामा निमिट्यान्न पारेर जान्छ । भदौ १० गते विभिन्न बस्तीहरूमा यस्तै अकल्पनीय र विनाशकारी विपद् आइलाग्यो । रसुवा र नुवाकोटमा दर्जनौँ बस्ती क्षणभरमै पूर्णरूपमा बगायो ।

बाढीले सयौँ नागरिकको पुस्तौँदेखि बसोबास गर्दै आएको थातथलो, उर्बर खेतीयोग्य जमिन बगायो । कयौँका आफन्त बाढीले आँखै अगाडि चुँडेर लग्यो ।

हिजोसम्म आफ्नै घरको आँगनमा भविष्यको तानाबाना बुनिरहेका रसुवाका नागरिक आज छिमेकी जिल्ला नुवाकोटको विदुर नगरपालिका-५ स्थित पिपलटार र कोदोबारीमा अस्थायी होल्डिङ सेन्टरहरूमा त्रिपालमुनि शरण लिन बाध्य छन् । आफ्नो सर्वस्व गुमाएका यी नागरिकहरूको वर्तमान जति कष्टकर छ, भविष्य त्योभन्दा पनि बढी अनिश्चित र कहालीलाग्दो देखिन्छ ।

नेपाल प्रेस ले यी होल्डिङ सेन्टरहरूमा पुगेर गरेको स्थलगत अध्ययन, प्रभावितका पीडा र भोगाइको अवलोकन, जनप्रतिनिधिहरूसँगको संवादलगायतको वस्तुस्थिति विश्लेषण गरेको छ ।

रसुवाका बाढीपीडितहरूलाई तत्काल आपत्कालीन राहत, गाँस र बासको प्रबन्ध मिलाउन नुवाकोटको विदुर नगरपालिका, नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी, सेभ द चिल्ड्रेन र विश्व खाद्य कार्यक्रमजस्ता संस्थाहरूको संयुक्त सहकार्यमा दुईवटा होल्डिङ सेन्टर सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएका छन् ।

पिपलटारको होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा उत्तरगया गाउँपालिकाको खाल्टेका बाढी प्रभावितलाई राखिएको छ। यहाँ कुल ३० वटा टेन्टमा १२० जना बसिरहेका छन् । राहत वितरण गर्ने संस्थाहरूले रासन उपलब्ध गराउँछन् र प्रभावितहरूले आ-आफ्नो समूह बनाइ एकै परिवार जस्तै आफैँ पकाएर खान्छन् ।

नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीकी स्वयंसेवक ऐश्वर्या पुडासैनीका अनुसार यस सेन्टरमा बालबालिका र महिलाहरूको मानसिक स्वास्थ्यलाई मध्यनजर गर्दै उनीहरूलाई सहज बनाउन र मनोसामाजिक परामर्श (काउन्सिलिङ) प्रदान गर्न छुट्टै ‘महिला मैत्री केन्द्र’ समेत स्थापना गरिएको छ ।

अर्का रेडक्रसकर्मी ऋषि रिजाल यहाँ राखिएकाहरूलाई स्वयंसेवकले पिउने पानी, रासन, त्रिपाल तथा भान्सा व्यवस्थापनको निरन्तर समन्वय गरिरहेका छन्। सुरक्षा संवेदनशीलतालाई ध्यानमा राख्दै बाहिरी अनाधिकृत व्यक्तिहरूको प्रवेश रोक्न सेन्टरको वरिपरि बाँसको बार लगाइएको छ र मुख्य गेट निर्माण गरिएको छ ।

पिपलटारभन्दा केही पर कोदोबारी होल्डिङ सेन्टर रहेको छ । विदुर-५ का वडाध्यक्षको निजी जग्गा भाडामा लिएर झाडी र पाक्न लागेको कोदोको बोट फाँडेर आपत्कालीन रूपमा सेन्टर सञ्चालनमा ल्याइयो

यहाँ रसुवाको आमाछोदिङ्मो गाउँपालिकासहित बाढीग्रस्त क्षेत्रका ७७ घरपरिवारका २७३ जना सदस्यलाई राखिएको छ । यस सेन्टरमा विश्व खाद्य कार्यक्रमको सहयोगमा सामूहिक मेस चलाइएको छ, जहाँ सबैका लागि सामूहिक रूपमा खाना पकाइन्छ र वितरण गरिन्छ ।

नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी नुवाकोटका प्रतिनिधि विनोद लामिछानेका अनुसार यहाँको जनसङ्ख्या धेरै भएकाले स्वास्थ्य जोखिम पनि उच्च छ । त्यसैले, चौबीसै घण्टा सेवा दिने गरी एम्बुलेन्स र ५-६ जना तालिमप्राप्त स्वयंसेवकहरूलाई तयारी अवस्थामा राखिएको छ । साथै, सुरक्षित खानेपानी, अस्थायी शौचालय, धारा र प्राथमिक स्वास्थ्य उपचारको पर्याप्त प्रबन्ध मिलाउने प्रयास गरिएको छ ।

उत्तरगया गाउँपालिका- १ का उचङ आलेको अनुहारमा बाढीले मानिसलाई कतिसम्म निरीह बनाउँछ भन्ने भाव प्रष्ट झल्किन्छ । श्रीमती, छोराबुहारीसमेत गरी उनको परिवारका ४ जना सदस्य आँखाअगाडि बाढीले बगायो ।

उनी भन्छन्, ‘मेरो आँखै अगाडि सबैलाई लग्यो । बचाउन अन्तिमसम्म तानेँ, तर पानीको भेल यति ठूलो थियो कि हात खुस्केर गयो । उनीहरूलाई पानीले निल्यो, म हेरेको हेरै भएँ ।’

झण्डै १ सय भेडा पालेर राम्रै जीवनयापन गरिरहेका उनको गोठ पनि बाढीले लग्यो । भाग्यवश बचेका केही भेडाहरू गाउँमै सस्तोमा बेच्नुपर्यो र अहिले एक्लै त्रिपालको आश्रयमा दिन काटिरहेका छन् ।

‘अहिले न मेरो घर छ, न भेडा छन्, न त मैले टेकेको माटो नै बाँकी छ । बाढीले सबै बगाएर बगर बनाइदियो,’ काम गर्न पनि मन लाग्दैन अब त ।

काठमाडौंमा १२ कक्षा पढिरहेका सुब्बा तामाङ बाढी आउँदा काठमाडौंमै थिए । उनी समाचार सुन्नासा गाउँ फर्किए । उनको परिवारसहित सिङ्गो गाउँ भूकम्पपछि नुवाकोटको बेत्रावती नजिकैको साल्ती र खाल्टेमा सरेको थियो ।

तर, नियतिको खेल बल्लबल्ल बसालेको नयाँ बस्ती पनि पूर्ण रूपमा बाढीले बगायो । तामाङका कान्छा काकाको परिवारका ५ जनामध्ये ४ जना र दुईटी फुपूको परिवारका ४ जना गरी ८ जना आफन्तले ज्यान गुमाए ।

‘भूकम्पपछि गाउँ छाडेर यहाँ बस्यौँ, शून्यबाट जीवन सुरु गरेका थियौँ । तर अहिले बाढीले त्यो पनि सिध्यायो,’ उनी भन्छन्, ‘आफन्तहरू धेरै गुमायौँ । हिजो भर्खर गएर पुरानो गाउँ हेर्न जाँदा भूगोल नै पुरै उल्टिएको छ । घर भएको ठाउँमा खोला बगेको छ । नमिठो सपना जस्तै लाग्छ ।’

बाढी आएका बेला रसुवाका धेरैजना रोजगारी वा व्यापारको सिलसिलामा चीनको केरुङ पुगेका थिए । तीमध्ये एक स्थानीय वृद्धाको अनुभव झनै कष्टकर छ । रसुवागढी नाकाको मितेरी पुल र सडक सञ्जाल बगाएपछि उनी चीनतर्फ नै थुनिइन् ।

उनी ल्हासा र सिन्धुपाल्चोक हुँदै गाडी र पैदल यात्रा गरेर ६-७ दिनको निरन्तर कष्टकर यात्रापछि मात्र नुवाकोट आइपुगिन् । आफ्नो परिवार जीवितै देख्दा राहतको सास फेरिन् । अहिले उनी आफ्ना ७ जना परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग एउटै त्रिपालमुनि आश्रय लिइरहेकी छन् ।

कोदोबारी सेन्टरमा बसिरहेकी याङजिन तामाङ गाउँबाट भाग्दा ज्यानसँगै जोगाएर ल्याएको पुरानो धागो र सियोबाट परम्परागत पहिरन ‘कुने’ (महिलाहरूले कपडाको पछाडि बाँध्ने विशेष प्रकारको कपडा) बुनेर मन बहलााइरहेको भेटिइन् ।

होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा नेपाल रेडक्रस, विदुर नगरपालिका लगायतका मानवीय संघसंस्थाहरूले गाँस र बासको तत्कालीन प्रबन्ध गरे तापनि त्रिपालको बसाइ जति दिन लम्बियो, त्यति नै नयाँ समस्याहरू थपिँदै गएका छन् ।

बाढीले घरसँगै बालबालिकाको विद्यालय र किताबकापी पनि बगायो । होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा रहेका स्कुल जाने उमेरका बालबालिकाहरूको पढाइ नबिग्रियोस् भनेर उनीहरूलाई नजिकैका स्थानीय विद्यालयमा भर्ना गराई पढाउन पठाइएको छ ।

सेभ द चिल्ड्रेन र रेडक्रसको सहजीकरणमा केही स्वयंसेवकले बिहान र बेलुका १-१ घण्टा बालबालिकालाई त्रिपालमुनि अतिरिक्त कक्षा पढाउने र गृहकार्य गराइरहेका छन् ।

स्वयंसेवक एन्जला तामाङ भन्छिन्, ‘बालबालिकाहरू स्कुल त गएका छन्, तर घरमा आएर पढ्न किताब नै छैन। घरसँगै सबै किताब बगेकाले अभ्यास गर्न र होमवर्क गर्न निकै समस्या परेको छ ।’

यसबाहेक उनीहरू गम्भीर मनोसामाजिक आघातबाट गुज्रिरहेका छन् । असोज १० को त्यो भयानक रातको घटना सम्झँदा उनीहरू अझै तर्सिने, निद्रामा आत्तिने, चिच्याउने र अभिभावक वा साथीभाइ गुमाएको शोकमा एक्कासि भावुक हुने समस्या व्याप्त छ ।

त्रिपालको बसोबासका कारण सबैभन्दा बढी कष्ट महिला, किशोरी र सुत्केरीहरूले भोग्नुपरेको छ । रसुवाको चिसो हावापानीमा हुर्केका उनीहरूलाई नुवाकोटको तातो वातावरण त्यसै पनि कष्टकर छ । त्यसमाथि त्रिपालमुनिको साँघुरो र खुला वातावरणमा नुहाउन, शौच गर्न र कपडा फेर्न असहज मान्ने गरेका छन् । रेडक्रसले अलग्गै स्थानको व्यवस्था भने गरेको छ ।

पिपलटार होल्डिङ सेन्टरको नजिकैको सुँगुर फार्मबाट गर्मी र हावा चलेको समयमा त्यहाँबाट आउने तीव्र दुर्गन्धका कारण सास फेर्न सास्ती भइरहेको प्रभावितहरू बताउँछन् ।

चिसो मौसम सुरु भइसकेको छ । रातको समयमा शीत खस्ने र भुइँबाट चिसो आउने हुनाले त्रिपालमुनिको बसाइ अत्यन्तै जोखिमपूर्ण बन्दै गएको छ । बालबालिका र वृद्धवृद्धाहरू रुघाखोकी र निमोनियाको सिकार हुन थालेका छन् । रेडक्रसका प्रतिनिधि विनोद लामिछानेका अनुसार चिसोबाट बचाउन पुराना र पातला त्रिपालहरू बदलेर न्यानो टेन्ट तथा जस्तापाता (टिन) को अस्थायी छाप्रो निर्माणतर्फ पहल भइरहेको छ, तर स्रोतको अभावले यो काम द्रुत गतिमा अघि बढ्न सकेको छैन ।

होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा दिइएको अस्थायी राहतले तत्कालको गर्जो त टारेको छ, तर बाढीपीडितहरूको भविष्य चरम अनिश्चिततामा रुमल्लिएको छ । उत्तरगया गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्ष माधवप्रसाद अर्याल पुन: बस्ती बसाउन मिल्ने सार्वजनिक जग्गासमेत पालिकामा छैन । भूगोल नै क्षतविक्षत भएकाले पीडितहरूलाई साविककै ठाउँमा फर्काउन असम्भवप्रायः छ ।

यस विषम परिस्थितिमा, दातृ निकायको भर परेर मात्र पुग्दैन । राज्यका तीनै तहका सरकारले रणनीतिक रूपमा योजना अगाडि बढाउनुपर्छ ।

सरकारले तत्काल भौगर्भिक अध्ययन गरी सुरक्षित स्थान खोजी गरी एकीकृत बस्ती बनाउनुपर्ने, बाढीले नागरिकता, लालपुर्जा, विद्यार्थीका शैक्षिक प्रमाणपत्रलगायतका महत्वपूर्ण कागजात होल्डिङ सेन्टरमै घुम्ती शिविर चलाएर पुनः जारी गर्नुपर्छ ।

कृषियोग्य जमिन नभएकोले उनीहरूलाई विभिन्न सीपमार्फत् वैकल्पिक पेसातर्फ आकर्षित गर्नुपर्छ । जसका लागि सहुलीयतपूर्ण ऋण र बीउपुँजी अनुदानको रूपमा उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्ने सरोकारवालाले बताएका छन् ।

प्रभावित बालबालिकाहरूका लागि निःशुल्क शैक्षिक सामग्री र अभिभावक गुमाएकाहरूलाई उच्च शिक्षासम्म नि:शुल्क ग्यारेन्टी गर्नुपर्छ ।

नेपाल रेडक्रस नुवाकोटका अध्यक्ष हरि श्रेष्ठ परिवारका सदस्य गुमाएकाहरू गहिरो मानसिक आघात, शोक र भविष्यको चिन्ताले डिप्रेसन र एन्जाइटीको समस्या बढ्न थालेको बताउँछन् । यसलाई बेलैमैमा सम्बोधन गर्न आवश्यक रहेको उनको भनाइ छ ।

पिपलटार र कोदोबारी होल्डिङ सेन्टरमा पाएको आपत्कालीन आश्रय, भोजन र मानवीय सहायताले तत्कालीन राहत त दिएको छ । सँगसँगै राज्यको बलियो उपस्थिति, अभिभावकत्व र न्यानो भरोसाको खाँचो छ ।

आफ्नो जन्मथलो, पैतृक सम्पत्ति, जीवनभरको कमाइ र आफ्ना प्रियजनहरू गुमाएर चरम अनिश्चित भविष्यको सामना गरिरहेका यी नागरिक अहिले राज्यको मुख ताकेर बसेका छन् । उनीहरूका लागि तत्काल स्थायी पुनर्वास, भू-स्वामित्वसहित जग्गा व्यवस्थापन, जीविकोपार्जनको ग्यारेन्टी गरिनुपर्छ ।

Bidur (Nuwakot). It is said that disaster does not come with a bang. But, when it comes, it wipes out the civilization, wealth and dreams created over generations in one fell swoop. On Bhadra 10, such an unimaginable and devastating disaster struck various settlements. Dozens of settlements in Rasuwa and Nuwakot were completely swept away in an instant. The flood washed away the fertile farmlands and homes where hundreds of citizens had lived for generations. Many relatives were swept away before their eyes. The citizens of Rasuwa, who were weaving the fabric of their future in their own backyards until yesterday, are now forced to take shelter under tarpaulins in temporary holding centers in Pipaltar and Kodobari, located in Bidur Municipality-5 of the neighboring district of Nuwakot. As difficult as the present is for these citizens who have lost everything, the future seems even more uncertain and dire. Nepal Press has analyzed the situation through on-site studies conducted at these holding centers, observations of the pain and suffering of those affected, and dialogue with public representatives. Two holding centers have been put into operation in collaboration with Bidur Municipality of Nuwakot, Nepal Red Cross Society, Save the Children, and the World Food Program to provide immediate emergency relief, food, and shelter to flood victims in Rasuwa. The holding center in Pipaltar is housing flood victims from Khalte, Uttargaya Rural Municipality. A total of 120 people are living here in 30 tents. Relief organizations provide rations, and the affected people form their own groups and cook and eat like a family. According to Aishwarya Pudasaini, a volunteer at the Nepal Red Cross Society, a separate 'Women-Friendly Center' has also been established at this center to provide psychosocial counseling and to make children and women feel comfortable, keeping in mind their mental health. Another Red Cross worker, Rishi Rijal, is continuously coordinating the provision of drinking water, rations, tarpaulins and kitchen management by volunteers for those housed here. Keeping in mind the security sensitivity, a bamboo fence has been erected around the center to prevent the entry of unauthorized persons from outside and a main gate has been constructed. A little further from Pipaltar is the Kodobari Holding Center. The center was brought into operation on an emergency basis by renting the private land of the ward chairman of Bidur-5, uprooting bushes and ripening millet plants. This center houses 273 members of 77 households from flood-affected areas, including Amachodingmo Rural Municipality in Rasuwa. A communal mess is run at this center with the support of the World Food Program, where food is cooked and distributed collectively for everyone. According to Binod Lamichhane, representative of Nepal Red Cross Society Nuwakot, the health risk is also high due to the large population here. Therefore, an ambulance and 5-6 trained volunteers have been kept on standby to provide 24-hour service. In addition, efforts have been made to make adequate arrangements for safe drinking water, temporary toilets, taps and primary health care. The pain of seeing a family disappear before our eyes The face of Uchang Ale of Uttargaya Rural Municipality-1 clearly reflects the extent to which floods make people helpless. Four members of his family, including his wife, son and daughter-in-law, were swept away by the flood before his eyes. He says, "They all disappeared before my eyes. I pulled to the end to save them, but the water was so strong that my hand slipped. They were swallowed by the water, and I was stunned." His sheepfold, where he was earning a good living by raising about 100 sheep, was also washed away by the flood. Fortunately, the few remaining sheep had to be sold cheaply in the village and are now spending their days alone under the shelter of a tent. "Now I have neither a house, nor sheep, nor the soil I used to walk on. The flood washed everything away and turned it into a wasteland," he says, "I don't even feel like working anymore." Subba Tamang, who was studying in grade 12 in Kathmandu, was in Kathmandu when the floods hit. He returned to his village after hearing the news. His entire village, including his family, had moved to Salti and Khalte near Betrawati in Nuwakot after the earthquake. However, as fate would have it, the newly built settlement was completely swept away by the flood. Eight relatives, including four out of five members of Tamang's younger uncle's family and four members of his aunt's family, lost their lives. "We left the village after the earthquake and settled here, starting life from scratch. But now the flood has ended that too," he says. "We have lost many relatives. Just yesterday, when I went to see the old village, the geography was completely turned upside down. A river has flowed where the house used to be. It feels like a bitter dream." When the floods hit, many people from Rasuwa had reached Kerung, China, for employment or business. The experience of one of them, an elderly local woman, is even more painful. She was stranded on the Chinese side after the Miteri Bridge and road network at the Rasuwagadhi border were washed away. She reached Nuwakot only after 6-7 days of continuous and arduous journey by car and on foot via Lhasa and Sindhupalchowk. She breathed a sigh of relief when she saw her family alive. She is now sheltering under a tent with her 7 family members. Yangjin Tamang, who lives in the Kodobari Center, was found entertaining herself by weaving a traditional garment called a 'kune' (a special type of cloth that women tie at the back of their clothes) using old threads and needles she had brought with her when she fled her village. Although humanitarian organizations including the Nepal Red Cross and Bidur Municipality made immediate arrangements for food and shelter at the holding center, new problems have been added as the tents' stay has prolonged. The flood washed away the children's school and textbooks along with their homes. To ensure that the school-age children in the holding center do not suffer, they have been admitted to nearby local schools and sent to study. With the facilitation of Save the Children and the Red Cross, some volunteers are teaching extra classes and doing homework for children under a tent for 1 hour each in the morning and evening. Volunteer Angela Tamang says, "The children have gone to school, but they don't have any books to read when they come home. Since all the books have gone with them, it's been very difficult to practice and do homework." In addition, they are going through severe psychosocial trauma. When they remember the terrible night of Asosh 10, they still experience fear, sleeplessness, screaming, and sudden emotional outbursts in grief over the loss of a parent or friend. Women, adolescents and pregnant women have suffered the most due to living in tents. Having grown up in the cold climate of Rasuwa, the hot environment of Nuwakot is also difficult for them. Moreover, they find it uncomfortable to bathe, defecate and change clothes in the cramped and open environment under the tents. The Red Cross has arranged a separate place. Those affected say they are having difficulty breathing due to the strong odor emanating from the pig farm near the Pipaltar Holding Center during hot and windy weather. The cold season has begun. As frost falls at night and the ground is cold, staying under tarpaulins has become extremely risky. Children and the elderly are becoming victims of colds and pneumonia. According to Red Cross representative Binod Lamichhane, efforts are being made to replace old and thin tarpaulins with warm tents and temporary shelters made of tin sheets to protect against the cold, but this work has not progressed quickly due to lack of resources. The temporary relief provided at the holding center has alleviated the immediate crisis, but the future of the flood victims is shrouded in extreme uncertainty. Uttargaya Rural Municipality Chairman Madhav Prasad Aryal said that the municipality does not even have public land that can be used for resettlement. Since the geography itself is damaged, it is almost impossible to return the victims to their previous places. In this critical situation, relying solely on donor agencies is not enough. All three levels of government must strategically advance the plan. The government should immediately conduct a geological study, find a safe location, and build an integrated settlement. Important documents such as citizenship, red papers, and students' educational certificates should be reissued at the holding center by running mobile camps. Since there is no arable land, they should be attracted towards alternative professions through various skills. For this, stakeholders have said that concessional loans and seed capital should be provided in the form of grants. Free educational materials should be guaranteed for affected children and free higher education for those who have lost their parents. Hari Shrestha, president of Nepal Red Cross Nuwakot, says that those who have lost family members are experiencing increased depression and anxiety due to deep mental trauma, grief, and worries about the future. He says that this needs to be addressed promptly. The emergency shelter, food, and humanitarian assistance provided at Pipaltar and Kodobari Holding Centers have provided immediate relief. At the same time, there is a need for a strong state presence, guardianship, and warm trust. These citizens, who have lost their birthplace, ancestral property, life's earnings, and loved ones, and are facing an extremely uncertain future, are now looking to the state for immediate permanent resettlement, land management, including land ownership, and guaranteed livelihoods.

Nepal Press has analyzed the situation through on-site studies conducted at these holding centers, observations of the pain and suffering of those affected, and dialogue with public representatives.

Two holding centers have been put into operation in collaboration with Bidur Municipality of Nuwakot, Nepal Red Cross Society, Save the Children, and the World Food Program to provide immediate emergency relief, food, and shelter to flood victims in Rasuwa.

The holding center in Pipaltar is housing flood victims from Khalte, Uttargaya Rural Municipality. A total of 120 people are living here in 30 tents. Relief organizations provide rations, and the affected people form their own groups and cook and eat like a family.

According to Aishwarya Pudasaini, a volunteer at the Nepal Red Cross Society, a separate 'Women-Friendly Center' has also been established at this center to provide psychosocial counseling and to make children and women feel comfortable, keeping in mind their mental health.

Another Red Cross worker, Rishi Rijal, is continuously coordinating the provision of drinking water, rations, tarpaulins and kitchen management by volunteers for those housed here. Keeping in mind the security sensitivity, a bamboo fence has been erected around the center to prevent the entry of unauthorized persons from outside and a main gate has been constructed.

A little further from Pipaltar is the Kodobari Holding Center. The center was brought into operation on an emergency basis by renting the private land of the ward chairman of Bidur-5, uprooting bushes and ripening millet plants.

This center houses 273 members of 77 households from flood-affected areas, including Amachodingmo Rural Municipality in Rasuwa. A communal mess is run at this center with the support of the World Food Program, where food is cooked and distributed collectively for everyone.

According to Binod Lamichhane, representative of Nepal Red Cross Society Nuwakot, the health risk is also high due to the large population here. Therefore, an ambulance and 5-6 trained volunteers have been kept on standby to provide 24-hour service. In addition, efforts have been made to make adequate arrangements for safe drinking water, temporary toilets, taps and primary health care.

The face of Uchang Ale of Uttargaya Rural Municipality-1 clearly reflects the extent to which floods make people helpless. Four members of his family, including his wife, son and daughter-in-law, were swept away by the flood before his eyes.

He says, "They all disappeared before my eyes. I pulled to the end to save them, but the water was so strong that my hand slipped. They were swallowed by the water, and I was stunned."

His sheepfold, where he was earning a good living by raising about 100 sheep, was also washed away by the flood. Fortunately, the few remaining sheep had to be sold cheaply in the village and are now spending their days alone under the shelter of a tent.

"Now I have neither a house, nor sheep, nor the soil I used to walk on. The flood washed everything away and turned it into a wasteland," he says, "I don't even feel like working anymore."

Subba Tamang, who was studying in grade 12 in Kathmandu, was in Kathmandu when the floods hit. He returned to his village after hearing the news. His entire village, including his family, had moved to Salti and Khalte near Betrawati in Nuwakot after the earthquake.

However, as fate would have it, the newly built settlement was completely swept away by the flood. Eight relatives, including four out of five members of Tamang's younger uncle's family and four members of his aunt's family, lost their lives.

"We left the village after the earthquake and settled here, starting life from scratch. But now the flood has ended that too," he says. "We have lost many relatives. Just yesterday, when I went to see the old village, the geography was completely turned upside down. A river has flowed where the house used to be. It feels like a bitter dream."

When the floods hit, many people from Rasuwa had reached Kerung, China, for employment or business. The experience of one of them, an elderly local woman, is even more painful. She was stranded on the Chinese side after the Miteri Bridge and road network at the Rasuwagadhi border were washed away.

She reached Nuwakot only after 6-7 days of continuous and arduous journey by car and on foot via Lhasa and Sindhupalchowk. She breathed a sigh of relief when she saw her family alive. She is now sheltering under a tent with her 7 family members.

Yangjin Tamang, who lives in the Kodobari Center, was found entertaining herself by weaving a traditional garment called a 'kune' (a special type of cloth that women tie at the back of their clothes) using old threads and needles she had brought with her when she fled her village.

Although humanitarian organizations including the Nepal Red Cross and Bidur Municipality made immediate arrangements for food and shelter at the holding center, new problems have been added as the tents' stay has prolonged.

The flood washed away the children's school and textbooks along with their homes. To ensure that the school-age children in the holding center do not suffer, they have been admitted to nearby local schools and sent to study.

With the facilitation of Save the Children and the Red Cross, some volunteers are teaching extra classes and doing homework for children under a tent for 1 hour each in the morning and evening.

Volunteer Angela Tamang says, "The children have gone to school, but they don't have any books to read when they come home. Since all the books have gone with them, it's been very difficult to practice and do homework."

In addition, they are going through severe psychosocial trauma. When they remember the terrible night of Asosh 10, they still experience fear, sleeplessness, screaming, and sudden emotional outbursts in grief over the loss of a parent or friend.

Women, adolescents and pregnant women have suffered the most due to living in tents. Having grown up in the cold climate of Rasuwa, the hot environment of Nuwakot is also difficult for them. Moreover, they find it uncomfortable to bathe, defecate and change clothes in the cramped and open environment under the tents. The Red Cross has arranged a separate place.

Those affected say they are having difficulty breathing due to the strong odor emanating from the pig farm near the Pipaltar Holding Center during hot and windy weather.

The cold season has begun. As frost falls at night and the ground is cold, staying under tarpaulins has become extremely risky. Children and the elderly are becoming victims of colds and pneumonia. According to Red Cross representative Binod Lamichhane, efforts are being made to replace old and thin tarpaulins with warm tents and temporary shelters made of tin sheets to protect against the cold, but this work has not progressed quickly due to lack of resources.

The temporary relief provided at the holding center has alleviated the immediate crisis, but the future of the flood victims is shrouded in extreme uncertainty. Uttargaya Rural Municipality Chairman Madhav Prasad Aryal said that the municipality does not even have public land that can be used for resettlement. Since the geography itself is damaged, it is almost impossible to return the victims to their previous places.

In this critical situation, relying solely on donor agencies is not enough. All three levels of government must strategically advance the plan.

The government should immediately conduct a geological study, find a safe location, and build an integrated settlement. Important documents such as citizenship, red papers, and students' educational certificates should be reissued at the holding center by running mobile camps.

Since there is no arable land, they should be attracted towards alternative professions through various skills. For this, stakeholders have said that concessional loans and seed capital should be provided in the form of grants.

Free educational materials should be guaranteed for affected children and free higher education for those who have lost their parents.

Hari Shrestha, president of Nepal Red Cross Nuwakot, says that those who have lost family members are experiencing increased depression and anxiety due to deep mental trauma, grief, and worries about the future. He says that this needs to be addressed promptly.

The emergency shelter, food, and humanitarian assistance provided at Pipaltar and Kodobari Holding Centers have provided immediate relief. At the same time, there is a need for a strong state presence, guardianship, and warm trust.

These citizens, who have lost their birthplace, ancestral property, life's earnings, and loved ones, and are facing an extremely uncertain future, are now looking to the state for immediate permanent resettlement, land management, including land ownership, and guaranteed livelihoods.
